samples.summary: CliAuthStore's own spec was not updated for the new `cliState` field it now stores and returns
samples.evidence: `createState`/`consumeState` gained a third parameter and a `cliState` field (cli-auth.store.ts:30,52-57), but cli-auth.store.spec.ts still only calls `createState('browser', 9876)` and asserts `toEqual({ csrf, mode, port })` — which passes regardless because jest's `toEqual` ignores `undefined` properties. No test in the store's own spec round-trips a nonce or proves it survives the 5-minute TTL / single-use paths. The only cliState coverage is indirect, via github-auth.guard.spec.ts:89.

samples.summary: `files list` claims `--type` is validated before the dry-run branch, but unlike `docs list` and `sheets export` no test asserts that ordering
samples.evidence: files.ts:81-93 adds the same 'validated BEFORE the dry-run branch' contract that read-dry-run.test.ts pins for `docs list` (line 121, 'rejects an invalid --type BEFORE the dry-run branch') and `sheets export` (line 192). Grepping read-dry-run.test.ts for `--type` shows only `docs list` cases; the `files` entry in the `describe.each` block only exercises `list`/`get` happy paths, so reordering the files.ts branches would print a preview for an invalid `--type` with no test failing.

samples.summary: The CLI↔backend query-parameter contract (`cliState` out, `state` echoed back) is pinned only by string literals on each side, with no test spanning the seam
samples.evidence: `buildAuthorizeUrl` sends `cliState=` (login.ts:251) and the listener reads `state` (login.ts:362); the backend reads `req.query?.cliState` (github-auth.guard.ts:73) and echoes `&state=` (auth.controller.ts:146-150). Each side's tests hardcode its own literal (login-callback.test.ts:'carries the nonce on the authorize URL', auth.controller.spec.ts:232), so renaming either param on one side leaves every suite green while the login silently stops binding. No integration/contract test was found covering both.

samples.summary: The `%2e` alternatives in DOT_SEGMENT are unreachable and untested — no test would fail if they were deleted
samples.evidence: `DOT_SEGMENT = /^(?:\.|%2e){1,2}$/i` is tested against the value AFTER `encodeURIComponent` (url.ts:45-46), which escapes `%` to `%25`, so `%2e` can never appear in `encoded`. url.test.ts only exercises `'.'` and `'..'`, and http-client-paths.test.ts explicitly asserts `'%2e%2e'` is NOT refused (`documents/%252e%252e`). The doc comment claims the `%2e` forms are handled; nothing tests that claim because the branch is dead.

samples.summary: The `--range` branch of the new `sheets export` dry-run preview is untested
samples.evidence: sheets-export.ts:48-55 builds `?range=<encoded>` in the dry-run branch, mirroring HttpClient.getCells. read-dry-run.test.ts's 'sheets export' describe only covers the no-range case (`sheets export doc-1 out.csv --dry-run`), so a divergence between the previewed range encoding and the client's would not be caught here (the analogous `cells get` block does cover the range shape).

samples.summary: No test asserts the loopback listener is actually closed after a successful login, so a leaked listening socket would go unnoticed
samples.evidence: `authorizeInBrowser` closes the server in a `finally` (login.ts:208-212) and `close()` also clears the timeout (login.ts:471-474). Every test in login-callback.test.ts calls `srv.close()` itself in its own `finally`; the 'gives the browser and stderr the URL the listener will honour' test never probes the port after resolution to prove the listener stopped. Removing the `finally { close(); }` from authorizeInBrowser would leave the suite green.
searchedFor: packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts (full read of listener + hand-off describes)

samples.summary: The 'does not crash when the login fails before anyone awaits it' test has no assertion for the behavior it names — it relies entirely on vitest's implicit unhandled-rejection detection
samples.evidence: The test's only assertion is `await expect(srv.waitForCallback()).rejects.toThrow(/Login timed out/)`, which holds whether or not `callbackPromise.catch(() => {})` (login.ts:329) exists. The stated behavior — no unhandled rejection while the caller is still in `await import('open')` — is only caught if vitest's runner surfaces the unhandled rejection as a run failure, which is an implicit runner behavior rather than an assertion in the test.
searchedFor: packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts:'does not crash when the login fails before anyone awaits it'

samples.summary: 'prints the GET without fetching or writing the file' never asserts that no file was written
samples.evidence: The sheets-export dry-run test asserts only `getCells` was not called and the printed JSON; `writeFileSync` is not spied on, so the 'without ... writing the file' half of the title is unasserted. (It is implied by the early return, but the test cannot distinguish it.)

samples.summary: `expect(nonce).toHaveLength(43)` asserts a property of the test's own fixture, not of any code under review
samples.evidence: `nonce` is `randomBytes(32).toString('base64url')` created in the spec itself; the length assertion holds regardless of how `normalizeCliState` behaves. Harmless, but it is documentation dressed as an assertion.

samples.summary: Guard branch for a CLI request with a non-numeric or absent `port` is untested
samples.evidence: github-auth.guard.ts:76-77 requires `Number.isInteger(portNum)`; the spec covers a valid port, an out-of-range port ('80') and no-mode requests, but never `?mode=cli&port=abc` or `?mode=cli` with no port. Those fall through to the web branch and, notably, skip `normalizeCliState` entirely — so a malformed `cliState` on such a request is silently dropped rather than rejected, and nothing asserts either way.

mergedFrom.summary: Test 'does not crash when a callback arrives before anyone awaits it' cannot fail — the path it claims to cover no longer rejects

finding.summary: Test named "does not crash when a callback arrives before anyone awaits it" never exercises a rejection, so it cannot fail if the `callbackPromise.catch(() => {})` guard is removed
finding.evidence: The test hits `/callback?code=unbound` with no `state`. In login.ts:306-317 that branch writes a 400 and returns — it never calls `callbackReject`, and `settled` stays false. The only path that rejects `callbackPromise` is the 30s timeout (login.ts:373-385), which this test never triggers (it waits 50 ms and asserts the promise is still pending). So the pre-attached `callbackPromise.catch(() => {})` added at login.ts:259 — the whole behavior the test's comment claims to protect ("a rejection raised in that window must not surface as an unhandled rejection") — is never exercised. Deleting line 259 leaves this test green. There are no fake timers anywhere in the file (no `vi.useFakeTimers`), so no other test covers it either.

finding.summary: No test covers the `login` action body: nonce minting, `--allow-unbound-callback` wiring into `startCallbackServer`, or that `open()`/stderr receive `startUrl` rather than the nonce-carrying authorize URL
finding.evidence: The only test of the command is `registerLoginCommand` → `expect(login?.options.map(o => o.long)).toContain('--allow-unbound-callback')`, which asserts the option exists but nothing about its effect. The action (login.ts:22-83) is where `randomBytes(32)` is minted, `allowUnbound: localOpts.allowUnboundCallback === true` is passed, `setAuthorizeUrl(buildAuthorizeUrl(...))` is called and `open(startUrl)`/`console.error(startUrl)` happen. If the action passed `state` to `open()` (the leak this change exists to prevent), or wired the flag to the wrong option name (commander camel-casing), every test in the file would still pass, because they all call `startCallbackServer`/`buildAuthorizeUrl` directly with hand-built arguments. Searched packages/cli/test for `allowUnbound`, `open(`, `startUrl` — only helper-level uses.

mergedFrom.summary: The new timeout message selection (version-skew message when a nonce-less callback was seen) has no test

finding.summary: The changed timeout behavior — reporting UNBOUND_CALLBACK_MESSAGE instead of the generic timeout when only nonce-less callbacks were seen — has no test
finding.evidence: login.ts:373-385 now branches the rejection message on `sawUnboundCallback`. No test triggers the 30s timeout: login-callback.test.ts uses only `settledWithin(..., 50)` (which resolves to `null` on non-settlement) and never installs fake timers, and `UNBOUND_CALLBACK_MESSAGE` is asserted only as a 400 response body (line ~99), never as the rejection reason. The version-skew signal the doc comment calls the point of the design is therefore untested.

glob packages/cli/test/** for a login action test
finding.summary: No test covers login.ts's actual hand-off: that `open()` and stderr receive `startUrl` and not the nonce-bearing URL
finding.evidence: The test titled 'keeps the nonce out of the URL handed to the browser and to stderr' (test line 184) only inspects the `startUrl` string returned by `startCallbackServer` and the `/start` redirect. It never touches the login action handler, so the security property it names — login.ts:66-72 printing `startUrl` and passing `startUrl` (not `buildAuthorizeUrl(...)`) to `open()` — is untested: swapping line 67 or line 72 back to the nonce-carrying URL would break the stated guarantee with every test still green. The only test of the action-registering function (test line 226) asserts merely that the command and the `--allow-unbound-callback` option exist, which says nothing about the hand-off.
